items.t: Nokia Shares Gain 3.5% as AI Networking Momentum Meets a Moody's Upgrade
sum: Nokia's stock closed Friday at €7.00, up 3.5%, as optimism around AI-driven telecom equipment and rising network traffic lifted sentiment. Media reports point to that broader enthusiasm as a possible backdrop for the move, though no single fresh catalyst has been confirmed as the trigger.

The advance followed a rebound in AI-related equities, which came on the heels of a two-day selloff, according to media accounts. Worries about spending levels in the AI sector and the prospect of regulation have not dissipated.

Roughly two weeks ago, Nokia reported third-quarter 2026 comparable net sales of €5,154 million, a 10% increase year over year by the company's own accounting. Comparable operating profit climbed 35% to €605 million. Management left its full-year outlook for comparable operating profit untouched, still projecting between €2.1 billion and €2.6 billion.

Among the week's concrete announcements, Hotwire Communications selected Nokia to construct a next-generation network in North Carolina. The build is designed to be ready for AI-based network architectures and will use Nokia's 7750 Service Router line. Activation is expected in early 2027. The order has not been established as the cause of the recent share-price gain.

Credit quality also moved in Nokia's favor this week. Moody's Ratings raised the company's long-term issuer rating and the rating on its senior unsecured obligations from Ba1 to Baa3, with the outlook remaining positive, according to media reports. The agency cited demand for cloud and AI infrastructure as well as Nokia's expanding network infrastructure business as the rationale.

Separately, Nokia published a long-range outlook on global network traffic. It projects that AI will account for 44% of worldwide network traffic by 2035, with total monthly data volume approaching 3,789 exabytes. The figures represent a corporate forecast rather than traffic volumes already recorded. While the Hotwire contract covers a specific build-out, the traffic report sets out Nokia's view of longer-term demand; early 2027 remains the next milestone on the North Carolina timeline.
Nokia and ICEYE also signed a letter of intent with Ukraine's defense ministry about two weeks ago. The parties will examine potential cooperation on sovereign satellite communications.

Danaos stock: Moody's lifts outlook to positive, notes to Ba1
sum: Danaos Corporation said on October 26, 2026, that Moody's Ratings had changed the outlook on its Ba1 Corporate Family Rating to positive from stable and upgraded its senior unsecured notes to Ba1 from Ba2. The company described the action in a Danaos Corporation investor release.

Moody's attributed the outlook change to higher revenue visibility, substantial cash balances and continued financial discipline. The rating agency also cited Danaos' long-term, fixed-rate charter portfolio, positive free cash flow track record and focus on reducing debt ahead of shareholder distributions.

As of June 30, 2026, Danaos had contracted revenue of approximately 4.6 billion US dollars, with an average remaining charter duration of 4.7 years. Cash stood at approximately 1.0 billion US dollars at that date, according to the company release.

Danaos' contracted charter base provides a degree of revenue visibility even if charter-market conditions weaken. That does not remove exposure to shipping cycles, but fixed-rate contracts can moderate the effect of short-term market swings on operating cash flow.
The real-time quote of Danaos stock was 135.60 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 23:00 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 2026.

Danaos is one of the largest independent owners of modern containerships and charters vessels to major liner companies on long-term agreements. Its fleet included 78 containerships with aggregate capacity of 502,265 TEUs, alongside 28 containerships under construction with capacity of 177,776 TEUs, according to the company release.

The company also has dry bulk exposure through 11 Capesize vessels and four Newcastlemax newbuildings. Danaos is headquartered in Cyprus and its shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker DAC.

items.t: Oracle stock slides as it borrows another $10 billion for AI spending
sum: Five days after Oracle (ORCL) promised to rein in its fundraising, it raised the full $20 billion in a single day.

Oracle kicked off a $10 billion bond sale Monday and, at the same time, filed to sell $10 billion of stock. Together, that's every dollar of new debt and stock it said at last week's investor day it would raise through fiscal 2030.

Investors didn't love the speed. Oracle stock fell nearly 9% Monday, its worst day since June, to its lowest close since July 29. That wiped out what was left of last week's 11% investor-day pop. Over three sessions, Oracle is down nearly 18%, its worst three-day stretch since 2002, by Yahoo Finance's calculations.

It's been a rough year. Oracle has lost more than half its value over the past 12 months, while Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOGL), and Meta (META) are all within about 5% of where they started.
So is Oracle Big Tech's canary in the coal mine? Not really.

The company's big drops haven't been an early warning for the rest of the group. After Oracle's nine previous three-day plunges of 12% or more since 2016, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta fell over the following month only four times, by Yahoo Finance's calculations. And at the tops of the dot-com bubble in 2000 and the pandemic boom in 2021, Oracle peaked after the Nasdaq, not before.
What sets Oracle apart is how it pays for the AI build-out. Follow the debt.

Editorial: It’s time for us to take stock of two elections
sum: As voters, we don’t always know who the candidates are or who will deliver on their promises. Often, it’s hard to connect with the contenders directly — the people who, if elected, will oversee policy and control the public purse.
In B.C., we’ve just come off back-to-back votes, so there’s been a lot of political messaging to wade through both municipally and provincially.
Let’s take a minute to catch our collective breath and review what we’ve just gone through.

On the civic front, we’ve got three new mayors in the seven communities we serve. And the provincial race ushered in a blue tsunami, with the Conservative Party of BC clinching three of the four seats in the Tri-Cities and two of the five in Burnaby.

In her last meeting as a city councillor, Trish Mandewo, who ran for the Coquitlam mayor’s chair, wept as she described the attacks against her during the seven-week race. She spoke about how her 22-year-old daughter had to hide the social media hatred so her mom could focus on running for public office.
MLAs also complained to Freshet News about the rage farming during the provincial campaign — digital posts designed to stir anger, outrage and fear.
We were told we would be a more caring, empathetic society in a post-pandemic world.

JPMorgan cuts Moody's target to USD 555 for Moody's stock
sum: JPMorgan Chase & Co. reduced its price target for Moody's from USD 570.00 to USD 555.00 on October 14, 2026, while retaining an Overweight rating, according to MarketBeat. The revision arrives one week before Moody's next quarterly report.

The lower target contrasts with Moody's latest reported operating picture. In the second quarter of 2026, revenue reached USD 2.19 billion, an increase of 15.10 percent from the same period a year earlier, while diluted earnings per share came to USD 5.03, according to MarketBeat. The company also set fiscal 2026 earnings-per-share guidance at USD 16.50 to USD 17.00.

For investors, the key test is whether the coming report supports that earnings path. MarketBeat cited a consensus target of USD 555.74 and a Moderate Buy rating, but those figures combine different analyst views and do not remove the questions reflected in the latest target reductions.

On July 22, 2026, Moody's reported second-quarter revenue of USD 2.19 billion and diluted earnings per share of USD 5.03, according to MarketBeat. On October 7, 2026, Morgan Stanley cut its target from USD 512.00 to USD 470.00. On October 14, 2026, JPMorgan Chase lowered its target from USD 570.00 to USD 555.00, with both analyst actions reported by MarketBeat.

Moody's will release third-quarter 2026 results before the NYSE opens on October 21, 2026, followed by an earnings conference call at 9:00 a.m. ET. The date and call details were announced by Moody's Corporation on September 30, 2026.

Moody’s Q2 Revenue Grew 15%, Is MCO Stock Worth Buying at $471?
sum: For much of this year, investors have been wrestling with a simple question: is a company this tied to debt market activity really worth owning at 26 times forward earnings when corporate borrowing could slow at any moment?
That skepticism has kept Moody’s Corporation (MCO) stock down roughly 5.5% year-to-date even as the broader market has moved higher.

The Q2 results, reported July 22, made that caution look misplaced. Moody’s posted $2.185 billion in revenue, up 15% year-over-year, driven by a significant tailwind from surging debt issuance across virtually every category.

As the revenue chart below shows, quarterly revenue has been climbing steadily, and while consensus expects some seasonal softness in the back half of 2026, the trajectory heading into 2027 remains positive.
CEO Rob Fauber noted that customers are turning to Moody’s “to make consequential decisions with greater confidence” as capital markets grow more complex.

Leveraged loan issuance volume jumped 53%, investment-grade volume rose 17%, and the Public, Project and Infrastructure Finance segment saw rated issuance volume grow 44%, driven by data center and technology infrastructure financing.
The market had been pricing in a cyclical slowdown. Instead, Moody’s delivered the opposite.

Record $2 Trillion Issuance Quarter Lifts Moody’s Stock Past Every Estimate

Moody’s Corporation (MCO) posted second-quarter 2026 revenue of $2,185 million, up 15% year over year and 5% above the $2,083.17 million Street estimate, with adjusted diluted EPS of $4.68 clearing the $4.25 consensus by 10%. That print built on strength across both segments rather than a single line item. Adjusted EBITDA reached $1,208 million at a 55.29% margin, up 439 basis points from a year ago, while free cash flow hit $688 million, up 47% year over year.

The engine behind the quarter was Moody’s Investors Service (MIS), the ratings division, which rated more than $2 trillion of debt for a second straight quarter and grew transaction revenue 34%. MIS adjusted operating margin reached 68.3%, up 410 basis points, as the business absorbed record volume without adding cost at the same pace. CEO Rob Fauber framed the scale of the beat directly on the Q2 2026 earnings call: “We achieved 15% revenue growth. We grew adjusted operating income by 25%, expanded adjusted operating margin by 440 basis points to 55.3% and we grew adjusted diluted EPS by 31% to $4.68, and that’s a great progression from the top line to the bottom line.”

sum: Results exceed expectations as outlook disappoints investors

Moody's Corporation (NYSE:MCO) reported stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results on Wednesday, although investors focused on a slightly softer full-year earnings outlook that weighed on the stock.
The credit ratings and analytics company posted adjusted earnings per share of $4.68, comfortably ahead of the analyst consensus estimate of $4.21.
Revenue increased 15% year over year to $2.19 billion, surpassing Wall Street expectations of $2.07 billion.
Despite the earnings beat, Moody's shares slipped 0.35% in premarket trading after the company narrowed its full-year earnings guidance.
Management now expects adjusted earnings per share for 2026 to range between $16.50 and $17.00. The midpoint of $16.75 is slightly below the analyst consensus estimate of $16.78.

"Moody's delivered exceptional results in the second quarter, reflecting both strong execution and the growing importance of trusted, decision-grade intelligence in an increasingly complex world," said Rob Fauber, President and Chief Executive Officer.

- Expansion into broader analytics and AI powered data workflows can support higher earnings expectations. However, any slowdown in private credit fundraising and deployment, particularly in Asia Pacific, may weigh on how much investors are willing to pay for that growth.
- Moody's scores 1 out of 6 on the broader valuation checks, which leans expensive rather than a clear bargain at the current share price.
The issue now is whether Moody's recent share price levels are justified by its intrinsic value estimate or leave limited room for disappointment.

The Excess Returns model looks at how much profit Moody's earns on its equity base above the cost of that equity. For Moody's, the inputs imply a book value of $17.14 per share supporting stable earnings of $20.13 per share, against a cost of equity of $2.07 per share. That gap translates into an excess return of $18.06 per share, underpinned by an average return on equity of 76.99% and a stable book value estimate of $26.15 per share.

items.t: 2 Large-Cap Stocks Worth Your Attention and 1 We Avoid
sum: Large-cap stocks are known for their staying power and ability to weather market storms better than smaller competitors. However, their sheer size makes it more challenging to maintain high growth rates as they've already captured significant portions of their markets.

These trade-offs can cause headaches for even the most seasoned professionals, which is why we started StockStory - to help you find high-quality companies that can grow their earnings no matter what. That said, here are two large-cap stocks with attractive long-term potential and one whose existing offerings may be tapped out.
Founded in 1926, United Airlines Holdings (NASDAQ:UAL) operates a global airline network, providing passenger and cargo air transportation services across domestic and international routes.
- Sluggish trends in its revenue passenger miles suggest customers aren't adopting its solutions as quickly as the company hoped
- Operating margin of 9.1% falls short of the industry average, and the smaller profit dollars make it harder to react to unexpected market developments
- Projected 5.5 percentage point decline in its free cash flow margin next year reflects the company's plans to increase its investments to defend its market position
United Airlines is trading at $135.24 per share, or 15.1x forward P/E. Read our free research report to see why you should think twice about including UAL in your portfolio, it's free.
